description:
"Some people look at data and see numbers. We see a world full of problems waiting to be solved. Two minds, one mission, and a little ambition to change how we understand our planet. We're ARCHON. And we're just getting started."

— ARCHON
summary:
MONSOON PULSE studies environmental changes across Kerala's 14 districts using NASA satellite data from 2001 to 2024. Developed for NASA's "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge, it brings together five datasets covering rainfall, land surface temperature, vegetation, soil moisture and terrain.

Using Google Earth Engine, Python and web technologies, the platform analyses these observations to identify long-term environmental patterns. It also introduces two indicators: HMV (Heat–Moisture–Vegetation), which combines temperature, soil moisture and vegetation data, and RTE (Rainfall–Terrain Exposure), which examines extreme rainfall alongside terrain slope.

Statistical methods, including the Mann–Kendall test, Theil–Sen slope estimation and False Discovery Rate correction, help evaluate the observed trends.

The project presents its findings through interactive district-level visualizations. Its goal is to make satellite data easier to explore and help researchers, students and disaster-management teams better understand historical environmental changes across Kerala.
details:
MONSOON PULSE is a project focused on understanding how Kerala's environment has changed over the years. We studied all 14 districts of Kerala using satellite data covering the period from 2001 to 2024. The main aim is to bring different environmental observations together and make them easier to explore and understand.

The project uses NASA datasets to study rainfall, land surface temperature, vegetation and soil moisture. By looking at these factors together, we can get a better picture of the environmental changes taking place across different parts of Kerala. We also developed two indicators, HMV and RTE, to explore the relationship between heat, moisture, vegetation, extreme rainfall and terrain.

The platform presents the results through interactive graphs and district-level views. It also uses statistical methods to identify long-term trends and examine whether the observed changes are statistically significant. This helps users explore the data instead of relying only on general conclusions.

We hope MONSOON PULSE can be useful to students, researchers and people interested in Kerala's environment. It can help make satellite data more accessible and encourage a better understanding of regional environmental changes.

For development, we used NASA Earth-observation datasets, Google Earth Engine, Python, JavaScript and web technologies. The project is hosted through GitHub Pages.

One of the main things that makes MONSOON PULSE different is that it brings several environmental factors into a single platform focused specifically on Kerala. During development, we considered the availability of satellite data, differences in observation periods, missing values, district boundaries and the reliability of statistical results. The project focuses on understanding historical trends and providing an accessible way to explore them.
